Need to search first.I couldn't write the notes. After my first search, the research tool hit its usage limit and refused every further search and page fetch. I didn't get to read any commentary, so I have nothing sourced to put verse by verse. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, so I haven't filled any verses from my own knowledge.

**What I did get done**

My one search returned these relevant pages. I saw only their titles and addresses, not what they say, so I can't cite anything from them yet:

- Enduring Word, full-chapter commentary on 1 Samuel 14: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-samuel-14/
- Enduring Word, sermon on 1 Samuel 14:6–7, "It May Be that the Lord Will Work for Us" (Jonathan's faith, v. 6): https://enduringword.com/it-may-be-1-samuel-146-7-february-1-2022/
- Enduring Word, media on 1 Samuel 14:24–52, about the foolish oath and what came of it (vv. 24–26): https://enduringword.com/media/1-samuel-14-foolish-oath-consequences/
- Precept Austin's 1 Samuel 14 commentary, which usually gathers many older and modern commentators: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-samuel-14-commentary

**Still to research once the tool works again**

1. **Traditional reading:** Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com or studylight.org, plus the pages above.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, plus Reformed, Baptist, Lutheran and Pentecostal teachers on Jonathan's sign (vv. 8–10), Saul's use of the priest (vv. 18–19) and Saul's oath (v. 24).
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for the hard textual points (the ark or the ephod in v. 18, and the earthquake in v. 15), and Catholic, Orthodox and popular modern readings where the sites cover them.

If you ask me to carry on in a new request, I'll start by reading these pages and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point.
